description: EBLE is a Norwegian evaluation of residential buildings with low energy demand: 64 passive houses and 10 dwellings built to the TEK10 building code were studied to learn about solutions, the need for innovation and potential. The project was led by Judith Thomsen and the data were archived in 2017 by NSD, the Norwegian Centre for Research Data, now part of Sikt. The material includes interviews with 38 residents and with participants in the building process, raw data on energy use and indoor climate, and moisture levels in the construction. Among its findings, residents had high expectations of indoor climate and comfort in new buildings, and these were met in the evaluated projects. Coverage: 74 dwellings in Norway. Access: through the Sikt survey bank, under its access conditions. Licence: set by Sikt; DataCite records no licence. Caveats: a small set of new, efficient dwellings, not representative of the stock. Simulation uses are calibrating energy and indoor-climate models of passive houses and informing occupant assumptions for low-energy housing. Related records: the timber-framed wall hygrothermal measurements and the BIM4EEB sensor datasets.
